faqs.question: What is the best design and creative tool for agencies?
faqs.answer: Based on our comprehensive evaluation, Figma is the best design and creative tool for agencies in July 20. It earned a 4.8/5 rating and excels at meeting the specific needs of digital agencies managing multiple clients who need collaboration, white-labeling, and reporting.

faqs.question: How much does design and creative software cost for agencies?
faqs.answer: design and creative tools for agencies range from free tiers to enterprise plans. Figma starts at Free – $75/mo per editor, while budget-friendly alternatives starting from lower price points are available.

faqs.question: What features should agencies look for in design and creative software?
faqs.answer: When evaluating design and creative tools for agencies, prioritize design capabilities, collaboration, prototyping. These factors most directly impact daily productivity and return on investment for agencies teams.

faqs.question: Can agencies use free design and creative tools effectively?
faqs.answer: Yes, several design and creative platforms offer generous free tiers suitable for agencies. We recommend testing free versions to evaluate fit before committing to paid plans.

faqs.question: What is the easiest design and creative tool for agencies to implement?
faqs.answer: Implementation difficulty varies, but Figma is known for straightforward setup, making it an excellent choice for agencies teams that want to get started quickly.

faqs.question: How do I choose between different design and creative tools for agencies?
faqs.answer: Consider your team size, budget, technical expertise, and specific workflow needs. Our comparison table above shows how each top pick stacks up across key criteria.

faqs.question: Are there design and creative tools designed specifically for agencies?
faqs.answer: Yes, many design and creative platforms offer features tailored to agencies. Our reviews detail which tools work best for different types of agencies teams.

faqs.question: How often should agencies review their design and creative tool choice?
faqs.answer: We recommend evaluating your design and creative stack annually or when your team grows significantly. The software landscape evolves rapidly with new features and entrants.

body:
Design and Creative Software for Agencies: Buyer Guide

Creative agencies need software that supports the deliverables they actually produce: interface design, prototypes, campaign assets, image editing, video, brand templates or client presentations. A tool that works well for one job may be the wrong fit for another. Choose by workflow and handoff requirements rather than by an unverified ranking.

Shortlist by workflow

Figma: evaluate for collaborative interface design, prototypes, shared libraries and developer handoff. Test comments, component changes, version history and guest-client access.

Sketch: evaluate when the team’s interface-design workflow and supported platform fit the product. Confirm collaboration, file compatibility and the handoff process with the current product edition.

Adobe Creative Cloud: evaluate when the agency needs a broader set of creative applications. Specify which apps are essential; do not pay for a bundle without checking actual usage and licensing needs.

Affinity: evaluate for focused design or image-editing work where its supported formats and collaboration model meet the brief.

Canva: evaluate for repeatable brand assets and marketing content that clients or non-designers need to update. Test brand controls, approvals, export and guest access.

InVision: confirm current product availability and the exact capabilities offered before treating it as a candidate; product history and legacy references are not proof of current suitability.

Run a real client project through each candidate

  1. Import an existing asset or create a representative screen and component.
  2. Invite a reviewer with the least privilege required and collect feedback.
  3. Make a component or brand update and check version history.
  4. Export files for developers, print or campaign publishing as required.
  5. Archive the project and test whether another teammate can recover it.

Agency requirements checklist

  • Separate client projects and restrict access to the correct team.
  • Track feedback, approvals and revision rounds.
  • Manage shared libraries and control who can publish changes.
  • Support required export formats, file ownership and handoff.
  • Meet accessibility and brand-governance needs.
  • Allow staff and client access to be removed cleanly at project close.

Compare total cost and exit risk

Ask vendors to quote the same number of creators, editors, reviewers and guest clients, plus storage, shared libraries and required applications. Check whether guests require paid seats and whether clients can access files after a project ends. Verify licensing, current product status, export formats and renewal terms. Prices and ratings are not independently verified in this guide.

Decision rule

Choose the tool that completes the agency’s main workflow with the least friction while meeting client separation, version control and handoff requirements. Document any workflow that still requires a separate application and include that cost in the decision.
